scope: Structural audit of existing separately implemented 1R and 1T1R h-BN laws; no refit
input_interpretation: Existing default calibration and archived reports; not fresh raw measurement extraction

set_envelope_extrapolation.law: I_h(V,x)=(1-x) A_pre V exp(beta sqrt(V)) + x A_connected V**n
set_envelope_extrapolation.meaning: The local soft-state envelopes reverse their state-current ordering on bare-voltage extrapolation; merely removing the transistor is not a validated 1R model

reset_conductance_gap.meaning: The calibrated soft-state endpoint and archived hard-state scale differ; this does not prove different intrinsic physics or matched device geometry

old_1r_clipping_counterexample.assumption: Frozen fully formed h=1, Rhard at old default median; ideal static current compliance
old_1r_clipping_counterexample.meaning: Clipping I while retaining commanded V as h-BN stress does not close the component law; a compliant source must solve actual V_h
old_1r_clipping_counterexample.limitation: The source workbook voltage column's command/readback semantics and instrument transient response are not established here

limitations: No experimental currents were fitted or scored in this audit.
No fresh XLSX data read was attempted; normal-operation first-three-cycle exclusion does not authorize deleting historical files.
No evidence here establishes matched 1R/1T1R cells, common geometry, paired bare SET/RESET cycles, or an identical parameter set.
Counterexamples assess the old models' mathematical scope, not the viability of all common h-BN mechanisms.
Different forming/history states may be legitimate, but independently resetting every branch is not state continuity.
